correctness.rationale: Under \(r=\theta^2\) and \(x=1\), the source boundary-law cubic and eigenvalue polynomial reduce exactly to \(F=0\) and spectrum \(\{1,0,\rho\}\) with \(\rho=y(\theta-y)/(2\theta+y^2)\). The Kesten–Stigum equality \(2\rho^2=1\) yields \(K=0\). A direct Sylvester determinant is \(16P\), and an exact rational Sturm sequence proves \(P\) has exactly two positive roots in the stated disjoint rational intervals. Algebra over \(\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)\) assigns the small root to \(\rho=-1/\sqrt2\) on the unique branch and the large root to \(\rho=+1/\sqrt2\) on the middle branch. Numerical values are not used for the infinite statements.

value.rationale: The two thresholds delimit sufficient non-extremality regions in the source and were left as computer decimals. Showing that both arise from one exact octic and from opposite-sign \(1/\sqrt2\) spectral crossings gives a structural description of the reconstruction boundary. The invariant is naturally selected by the Kesten–Stigum criterion and the source branch, rather than by an arbitrary numerical slice.
